note: Synthetic legal mini-gold set: 37 labeled documents. Twenty-three Turkish documents covering criminal, civil, commercial, enforcement, employment, medical (one of them typed without diacritics, whose diagnosis follows a "Doc. Dr." title), OCR-noisy, notary, KVKK, lease, and corporate documents, plus three bare-name documents where person names appear WITHOUT a title or party-role prefix (running text, attendee/witness lists, signature blocks), and five regression cases: a case-law opinion citing Yargıtay and Danıştay decisions with numbered chambers and E./K. case-number initials, a service agreement whose parties are named by role (Hizmet Veren, Hizmet Alan), an investigation note naming prosecutor's offices, courts and a notary with a genitive case ending (Başsavcılığının, Mahkemesinin, Noterliğinin) and citing investigation numbers in the forms that follow an office (2024/12345 sayılı soruşturma, 2023/9071 soruşturma numaralı, 2025/4410 Soruşturma No'lu), a file note citing investigation dockets (2024/12345 sayılı soruşturma dosyası, Soruşturma No: ... olan dosya, a Soruşturma Bürosu) beside two clauses that do allege an offence (... suçunu işlediği iddia edilen / edilmektedir), and a commercial note naming each company mid-clause, behind a party-role word or after ordinary clause words ("Sözleşme gereği Davalı taraf olan yıldızlı örnek holding a.ş.", "Alacaklı Yıldız LTD. ŞTİ."), whose company spans tests/test_company_span.py pins on offsets. Six English documents under tests/fixtures/english/: a UK witness statement, a letter before claim, an employment tribunal judgment, a US settlement agreement, and a Turkish annex carrying English witness details as labelled fields, and a standard contractual clauses execution page whose signature lines name the parties by role (Data Exporter, Data Importer). Three Turkish practice samples shipped in samples/documents/ (contract, enforcement file, notarial notice), measured as the .docx files the app loads. Five name documents under tests/fixtures/names/: two (one English, one Turkish) where a person named in full is referred to later by bare surname, with and without a case suffix or possessive, and named in full again in prose; and two where people are named in plain prose with given names only the official name lists (US SSA, ONS, TÜİK) carry, beside the homographs a bigger list must not read as people ("Kira Bedeli", "Kuzey Cephesi", "Hava Durumu", "Savaş Hali", "Duran Varlıklar", "Dönen Varlıklar", "London EC2R", "Will and testament", "Mercedes Benz", "Montana Ridge", "Geneva Convention"); "Barış Görüşmesi" is left as a known false positive, Barış being on the hand-written list. The English listed-names document also carries a bare surname after "the" ("The Ravensworth report"), and the Turkish surname document a bare surname, mid-sentence and opening a sentence, whose only lowercase form is a lowercase repeat of the full name ("ekin kartal"); the English surname document a sentence-opening bare surname whose only lowercase form is the person's e-mail address ("j.stanbridge@example.com"). All are still the person. The fifth, an English custodian list, names people whose given names no list carries in the two places a document spells a name for you: right before the e-mail address its local part spells ("Ottoline Quarrendon, ottoline.quarrendon@…", "Lysander Pellingham (l.pellingham@…)", "Hepzibah Wrexbridge <hepzibah_wrexbridge@…>") and on the signature line itself ("Signed: …", "Signed by … and …"), beside two team mailboxes that spell their address the same way and are not people because the document uses their words in lowercase ("records management", "data protection").
